name: Agentic Additive Manufacturing Alloy Evaluation (Claude Code multi-agent)

system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Each of these packages maintain their own MCP server tools andSub-agent 88 (a simple markdown file providing additional context and system prompts to guide tool usage)
system_prompt_style.note: Subagent markdown prompts composed per invoked subagent within Claude Code.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: Tools to list existing subfolders and their contents act as guides to help the LLM navigate through potential tool input arguments narrow the search win-dow to the most applicable candidates.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Since the lack of fusion regimes are returned as power and velocity combinations within a list of tuples

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Tools are the primary means in which an LLM is able to perform actions via MCP, invoking external Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) or function calls with the user's ap-proval.

tool_count.note: Tool counts across the three MCP servers are not enumerated in the paper or the pinned repo evidence.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: these tools can be exposed to the LLM with the appropriate decorator function configuration as seen in Appendix A
tool_schema_source.note: Hand-written title/description/docstrings on @app.tool decorators, served over MCP.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Multi-agent workflow configuration for additive manufacturing alloy evaluation via Model Context Protocol (MCP)

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: These agents can dynamically adjust their task trajectory to the outcomes of tool call results, effectively enabling autonomous decision-making in practical environments.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: The multi-agent system is able to reason and plan through given tasks and dynamically adjust task trajectories based on tool responses.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Claude Code 89 provides a platform for cou-pling these tools into a multi-agent environment utilizing Claude Sonnet 4 90 as the primary large language model for orchestrating tool calls

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Streamlined summary of tool executions and analysis from the prompt given to Claude Code utilizing subagents for Additive Manufacturing, Thermo-Calc, and Workspace.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: invoking external Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) or function calls with the user's ap-proval

short_term_state.evidence_quote: It primarily acts as a state management tool for storingJSONserialized class objects and deserializng the storedJSONfiles to use within tools.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Workspaces can be initialized via tool call (Figure 3) and are subdivided into top-level subfolders (i.e.compositions,materials,process maps, etc.) containing state and re-sponses for a given domain.
long_term_memory.note: Workspace JSON files persist on disk across sessions; not framed as memory.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: filename references to serializedJSONfiles are provided as inputs to be loaded and deserialized within each tool
state_persistence.note: Workspace state reloadable; no explicit conversation resume described.

self_verification.evidence_quote: In this agentic system, all tasks are completed with tools performing deterministic actions; the large language model merely orchestrates and analyses the response of dispatched tool calls.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: The one failure in this case occurred with the Tool Steel prompt which resulted in the process hanging while utilizing the property diagram calculation tool.
retry_policy.note: Failures reported, no retry mechanism described.

rollback.evidence_quote: It primarily acts as a state management tool for storingJSONserialized class objects
rollback.note: No undo/revert facility described in workspace state management.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Additionally, consideration towards optimizing token and time cost between various LLM providers will be incorporated as well.
